Getting Started with PocketRoute

15 min read Updated June 3, 2025 Applies to v2.0+

This guide walks you through setting up PocketRoute for your delivery team — from installing the app on driver devices to running your first optimized route. You'll be dispatching routes in under 15 minutes.

Requirements

Before you begin, make sure you have the following:

Account A PocketRoute account (any plan). Sign up free if you don't have one.
iOS iPhone or iPad running iOS 16.0 or later
Android Android 10.0 or later with Google Play Services
Web Modern browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari 16+) for the dispatcher dashboard
Connectivity Internet connection required; limited offline mode available on mobile
Note

The dispatcher dashboard and route creation tools are web-based. Drivers only need the mobile app — they never need to access the web interface.

1. Install the App

PocketRoute has two components: the Dispatcher Dashboard (web, used by you) and the Driver App (mobile, used by your drivers). Start by downloading the driver app on at least one device to test with.

App Store (iOS)
Google Play (Android)
1

Search for "PocketRoute" in your app store

The app is published by PocketRoute, Inc. Look for the amber route icon. Download is free — drivers don't need a paid account.

2

Grant location and notification permissions

PocketRoute requires Always On location access to track driver positions in real time. Notification permission is needed to receive route assignments. Both prompts appear on first launch.

3

Sign in or accept your team invitation

Drivers sign in using the invitation email you send them (covered in Step 3). If testing with your own device, sign in with your account credentials.

Important

On iOS, choosing "Allow Once" for location instead of "Always Allow" will cause the app to lose tracking when backgrounded. Drivers must select "Always Allow" for accurate dispatch.

2. Create Your First Route

Routes are created in the web dashboard at app.pocketroute.io. Log in and navigate to Routes → New Route.

1

Add a start location

This is your depot, warehouse, or pickup point. Type an address or drop a pin on the map. PocketRoute uses this as the route origin and return point.

2

Add delivery stops

Type addresses one by one, paste a list, or import from CSV. Each stop can have a recipient name, delivery notes, time window, and priority level. You can add up to 250 stops per route on the Growth plan.

3

Run route optimization

Click Optimize Route. PocketRoute's algorithm reorders your stops to minimize total drive time, respecting time windows and priority flags. Optimization typically completes in under 10 seconds for routes under 100 stops.

4

Assign to a driver and dispatch

Select a driver from your team (or assign to yourself for testing), then click Dispatch. The driver receives a push notification and the route loads automatically in their mobile app.

CSV Format addresses.csv — import template 
address,recipient,notes,time_from,time_to
"123 Main St, Brooklyn, NY 11201","Sarah Chen","Leave at door","09:00","12:00"
"450 Park Ave, New York, NY 10022","James Rivera","Buzzer 4B","10:00","14:00"
"88 Pine St, Jersey City, NJ 07302","Delivery Desk","","",""

3. Invite Your Team

Add drivers from the Team section of your dashboard. Each driver gets their own account — you never share credentials.

1

Go to Team → Invite Driver

Enter the driver's email address and set their role. The Driver role lets them receive and complete routes but not create them. The Dispatcher role adds route creation and team visibility.

2

Driver accepts the invitation

The driver receives an email with a secure link. On first sign-in, they set their own password. They're immediately added to your team and can receive dispatched routes.

3

Verify they appear on the live map

Once signed in with location permissions granted, you'll see the driver's position on the dispatcher map within 30 seconds of them opening the app.

Team Limits

The Starter plan supports up to 3 drivers. The Growth plan supports up to 15 drivers, and the Team plan is unlimited. Contact us if you need to temporarily exceed your driver limit.

4. Configure Notifications

PocketRoute sends notifications to keep you informed of route progress. Configure these under Settings → Notifications.

  • Route started — when a driver marks the first stop en route
  • Delivery confirmed — when a driver marks a stop as delivered or attempted
  • Route completed — when all stops are resolved and the driver returns to base
  • Driver delayed — when a driver is more than 10 minutes behind schedule (configurable)
  • Failed delivery — when a stop is marked as failed or undeliverable

Notifications can be sent via push, email, or SMS. SMS requires a phone number on your account and is available on Growth and Team plans.

5. Set Up Billing

If you're on the free trial, you have 14 days and up to 3 drivers on full features. Before the trial ends, add a payment method under Settings → Billing.
